title: Recording: A Love For You, Long Haired Lady by Paul and Linda McCartney | 1970
content:
Studio B, CBS Studio Building, New York City
Producers: Paul McCartney, Linda McCartney

Paul McCartney worked on two songs on 27 October 1970: ‘A Love For You’ and ‘Long Haired Lady’.

‘A Love For You’ had been worked on during the previous day’s session. The basic track featured McCartney on his Martin D-28 acoustic guitar and guide vocals, joined by session guitarist Hugh McCracken and drummer Denny Seiwell.

McCartney reportedly planned to issue the song as a single, with ‘Get On The Right Thing’ on the b-side, but it was cancelled after the formation of Wings.

The recording was revived in October 1980 during the final Wings days, at Rude Studio in Campbeltown, Scotland, while McCartney was working on the abandoned Cold Cuts project. The overdubs included guitar by Laurence Juber and percussion by Steve Holley.

Further work took place in 1986 and 2002, and the song was eventually included in the soundtrack of The In-Laws, a remake of the 1979 film of the same name. Jon Kelly’s 1986 mix of ‘A Love For You’ was included on the 2012 reissue of Ram.

In the afternoon McCartney led the session musicians through ‘Long Haired Lady’, which had the working title ‘Love Is Long’. Although they worked on the song for several hours, it was incomplete by the time Bob Dylan called in at the session.

That evening the McCartneys were invited to dine with Dylan, his wife Sara, and their five children at their apartment at 94 McDougal Street in Greenwich Village.

Page last updated: 8 November 2025
